content.directions: For this part you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "While striving for the Chinese Dream, young people enjoy more opportunities to realize their self-worth." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: Young people realizing self-worth while striving for the Chinese Dream

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话1。

transcript.text: I must say, I love our canteen.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我必须说，我喜欢我们的食堂。

transcript.text: It's such a great meeting point.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它是一个很棒的聚会点。

transcript.text: Yeah, it really is, both for students and teachers.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，确实如此，对学生和老师来说都是。

transcript.text: Shame about the food.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 食物方面有点遗憾。

transcript.text: What do you mean?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你什么意思？

transcript.text: I think the food is fine.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我觉得食物还行。

transcript.text: I would say the food is just OK.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我会说食物一般般。

transcript.text: But the prices are absurd.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但价格荒谬。

transcript.text: Don't you agree?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你不同意吗？

transcript.text: I don't, actually.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 实际上，我不同意。

transcript.text: I personally think they're perfectly appropriate.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我个人认为它们非常合适。

transcript.text: If it's overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunchtimes?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果价格过高，为什么午餐时间它会如此疯狂地忙碌？

transcript.text: You make a good point.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你说得有道理。

transcript.text: I guess a lot of it is good value.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我猜很多东西物有所值。

transcript.text: Maybe even most of it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 甚至可能大部分。

transcript.text: However, don't you think $6 for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students' budgets?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 然而，你不觉得一片苹果酥6美元超出了大多数学生的预算吗？

transcript.text: Yes, desserts are overpriced.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，甜点价格过高。

transcript.text: I'll give you that.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我同意你这一点。

transcript.text: To be honest, I've forgotten about those as I never eat them.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 说实话，我忘了那些，因为我从不吃它们。

transcript.text: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我从不渴望甜食或任何精致美食。

transcript.text: What I always go for is their scrambled eggs.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我总是点他们的炒蛋。

transcript.text: They have such a great variety.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 他们有如此多的种类。

transcript.text: Yeah, those are good.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，那些很好。

transcript.text: They also come out really fast.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它们上菜也很快。

transcript.text: Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 实际上，那是食堂最好的事情之一。

transcript.text: The speed.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 速度。

transcript.text: If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don't have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 如果我想要比三明治更丰盛的东西，但午餐时间不多，大学食堂总是一个好选择。

transcript.text: The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 厨房工作人员以如此快的速度工作。

transcript.text: They really deserve to be complimented for it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们真的因此值得称赞。

transcript.text: Totally.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 完全同意。

transcript.text: And it's such a great environment, too.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而且环境也非常棒。

transcript.text: Like, the entire building is beautiful.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 比如，整个建筑很漂亮。

transcript.text: It is very nice.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它非常不错。

transcript.text: The massive glass windows make all the difference.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 巨大的玻璃窗起了关键作用。

transcript.text: I think they're so cool.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我觉得它们很酷。

transcript.text: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 显然，他们几年前进行了一次大规模翻新。

transcript.text: It cost them a pretty penny.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这花了他们不少钱。

transcript.text: Yeah, I'm not surprised.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，我不惊讶。

transcript.text: It's a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这是一个非常多用途的空间，适合吃饭和放松。

transcript.text: And for working.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而且对于工作。

transcript.text: You're right.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你说得对。

transcript.text: Working, too.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 工作也是。

transcript.text: I've used my laptop there once or twice, and there's always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我在那里用过一两次笔记本电脑，而且远处总是有小组项目或会议在进行。

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话2。

transcript.text: Hi, Tony.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗨，Tony。

transcript.text: Today, we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 今天，我们讨论管理者如何在工作中与年轻人更好地相处。

transcript.text: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们经常听说今天的年轻人职业道德不佳。

transcript.text: That's not really justified, though, is it?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但这并不是真的合理，对吧？

transcript.text: Not really.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不完全是。

transcript.text: In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代一样多样化和多面。

transcript.text: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，但如果你在工作场所与年轻人合作有困难，你能做什么？

transcript.text: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，与他们建立联系以了解他们的价值观是至关重要的。

transcript.text: It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 同样重要的是认识到年轻人希望如何平衡工作生活与个人生活。

transcript.text: So, they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以，他们通常不想为了职业晋升而推迟幸福？

transcript.text: Absolutely.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 绝对如此。

transcript.text: They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives, and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们不愿意为了工作生活而牺牲个人生活，这导致人们将其等同于不愿意努力工作。

transcript.text: Right, but that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 对，但这与事实相去甚远，不是吗？

transcript.text: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights, free from work.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 年轻人会在规定的工作时间内非常努力地工作，但他们期望在休息时间，如周末和晚上，不受工作打扰。

transcript.text: So, how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那么，管理者应该如何评估年轻人的工作效率？

transcript.text: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for 8 hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 通常，年轻人认为他们的工作效率不应以工作时长来衡量，因为有人可能工作8小时却几乎没有为公司取得重要成果。

transcript.text: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 相反，年轻人通过他们工作的质量来衡量工作效率。

transcript.text: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但我们经常听说年轻人希望感受到的不仅仅是作为大机器的一部分。

transcript.text: Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这种观点很难被反驳，不是吗？

transcript.text: It's important to legitimize their work.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 重要的是使他们的工作得到认可。

transcript.text: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company, or the world at large.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 年轻员工希望从事对他们自己、公司或整个世界重要的项目。

transcript.text: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们必须感觉到有必要留在一家价值观与自己一致的公司工作。

transcript.text: Thanks for your advice.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 感谢你的建议。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 篇章1。

transcript.text: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.
transcript.translation: 许多餐馆试图说服顾客更可持续地饮食，从环境不友好的肉类转向更环保的菜肴。

transcript.text: Although it sounds counterintuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
transcript.translation: 一项新研究表明，尽管这听起来有违直觉，但菜单上设有特定素食区域的餐馆可能无意中鼓励了顾客吃肉。

transcript.text: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.
transcript.translation: 该研究作者之一、行为科学家琳达·培根表示，餐馆可以通过鼓励顾客选择更多植物性食物、减少肉类消费来对环境产生积极影响。

transcript.text: However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others.
transcript.translation: 然而，我们的研究结果表明，尽管某些餐馆菜单设计可以鼓励一些消费者做出环保的食品选择，但对其他人可能产生相反效果。

transcript.text: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it.
transcript.translation: 该研究涉及750人，其中一半人经常吃素食，另一半人很少吃素食。

transcript.text: No vegetarians were included.
transcript.translation: 没有包括素食主义者。

transcript.text: They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
transcript.translation: 他们被给予不同的菜单，并被要求选择一顿餐点，就像他们和朋友外出就餐一样。

transcript.text: Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters, but it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%.
transcript.translation: 将素食菜肴放在单独区域对不常吃素食的人的选择没有显著影响，但对经常吃素食的人有显著影响，将他们选择素食选项的几率降低了65%。

transcript.text: The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option.
transcript.translation: 研究人员还发现，将素食菜肴呈现为厨师推荐或对非肉食餐点添加更吸引人的描述，会导致更高比例的不常吃素食的人选择素食选项。

transcript.text: But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
transcript.translation: 但再次，这些改变的菜单设计对经常吃素食的人产生了适得其反的效果，导致他们更不可能选择素食菜肴。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 段落2。

transcript.text: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.
transcript.translation: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在寻找一种方法，以防止致命的室外空气污染渗入室内。

transcript.text: They found that if pollution is frozen to around minus 18 degrees Celsius in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh clean air to pass through.
transcript.translation: 他们发现，如果将污染在冷凝管中冷冻到约零下18摄氏度，颗粒会聚集在一起并沉到底部，从而让新鲜清洁的空气通过。

transcript.text: Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.
transcript.translation: 他们的方法能够去除99%的污染物。

transcript.text: It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
transcript.translation: 希望这项工作能为空调单元的简单改造铺平道路，使其也能清洁受污染的室内空气。

transcript.text: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Kolkata or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools.
transcript.translation: 城市中的室外空气污染是一个全球性问题，无论是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校儿童健康的空气污染。

transcript.text: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful byproducts.
transcript.translation: 虽然有一些现有的技术来净化室内空气，但它们可能效率低下、成本高昂或产生有害副产品。

transcript.text: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors, but outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution and people still suffer.
transcript.translation: 当室外空气质量差时，人们倾向于花更多时间在室内，但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人们仍然受害。

transcript.text: It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.
transcript.translation: 据估计，污染每年在英国与超过40,000例早逝有关。

transcript.text: Professor Gong Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
transcript.translation: 中国科学院的龚攀教授说，我们在实验中已经证明，只需将污染空气通过一个小型冷冻室循环，就能去除大部分细颗粒物和气体污染物。

transcript.text: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.
transcript.translation: 我们的研究使得在可能经历极端恶劣空气条件的地区，为家用电器添加空气净化选项成为可能。

transcript.text: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health.
transcript.translation: 通过以这种方式控制室内空气污染并改善空气质量，这项工作可能对公众健康大有裨益。

transcript.text: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware.
transcript.translation: 我的团队最近进行的研究表明，鱼可能具有自我意识。

transcript.text: A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
transcript.translation: 某种鱼最近通过了著名的镜子测试。

transcript.text: This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals.
transcript.translation: 这是一个展示动物自我识别能力的测试。

transcript.text: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins, and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror.
transcript.translation: 只有少数动物，如人类、猿、海豚和某些鸟类，能在镜子中认出自己。

transcript.text: And only these animals capable of self-recognition will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection.
transcript.translation: 只有这些具有自我识别能力的动物，才会在镜中注意到标记后试图去除皮肤上的标记。

transcript.text: This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness.
transcript.translation: 这种能力表明了一种更高层次的智力和意识。

transcript.text: This is not shown by children until around 18 months.
transcript.translation: 儿童直到大约18个月大时才表现出这种能力。

transcript.text: Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability.
transcript.translation: 直到现在，没有鱼表现出这种能力。

transcript.text: But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror.
transcript.translation: 但我们的实验显示，这种鱼会在看到镜中的自己后，通过刮擦硬表面来去除研究人员放在其身上的标记。

transcript.text: The behaviours we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviourally fulfils all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.
transcript.translation: 我们观察到的行为几乎没有疑问，这种鱼在行为上完全满足了最初设定的镜子测试的所有标准。

transcript.text: The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present, or when the marks were just placed on the mirror.
transcript.translation: 在我们的研究中，当没有镜子存在时，或者当标记只放在镜子上时，这种鱼从未试图去除标记。

transcript.text: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window.
transcript.translation: 没有标记的鱼在与另一侧的有标记鱼互动时，也没有试图去除自己身上的标记。

transcript.text: These results show either that fish are self-aware, or that the mirror test, which is considered to the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
transcript.translation: 这些结果表明，要么鱼具有自我意识，要么被认为是用于表示更高智力的黄金标准测试的镜子测试可能存在缺陷。

transcript.text: What is less clear is whether these behaviours should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past these same behaviours have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals.
transcript.translation: 不太清楚的是，这些行为是否应被视为鱼具有自我意识的证据，尽管过去同样的行为在许多其他动物中被解释为自我意识。

transcript.text: Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviours in a fish satisfy passing the test at all.
transcript.translation: 根据你的立场，你可能拒绝接受这种解释，即鱼的这些行为完全满足通过测试的条件。

transcript.text: But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviours they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
transcript.translation: 但当它们表现出的行为与通过测试的其他物种的行为在功能上如此相似时，你能基于什么客观依据这样做呢？

transcript.text: Results from our research raise more questions than answers.
transcript.translation: 我们的研究结果引发的问题比答案更多。

transcript.text: What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer, rather than appearing all at once?
transcript.translation: 如果自我意识像洋葱一样发展，一层一层地构建，而不是一次性出现，那会怎样？

transcript.text: Perhaps, in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test.
transcript.translation: 也许，为了进一步探索自我意识，我们应该停止将镜子反应视为决定性的测试。

transcript.text: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
transcript.translation: 只有拥有更丰富的自我理论和更广泛的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的所有不同层次，包括鱼究竟处于哪个位置。

transcript.text: Reading with a young child is important, but does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print?
transcript.translation: 与幼儿一起阅读很重要，但使用电子书还是传统印刷品阅读是否重要？

transcript.text: As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens, so the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise, but the following additional findings might.
transcript.translation: 正如任何父母所知，幼儿通常喜欢屏幕，因此一项新研究发现幼儿比印刷图画书更喜欢电子书，这可能不会让人感到太惊讶，但接下来的附加发现可能会。

transcript.text: Both parents and children behave differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books, and the children who read the electronic books learned more.
transcript.translation: 父母和孩子在阅读电子图画书与印刷图画书时行为不同，而且阅读电子书的孩子学到了更多。

transcript.text: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features, such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print.
transcript.translation: 先前关于幼儿的研究表明，电子书结合了额外功能，如词典和描绘故事事件的图像，可能比印刷品更具优势。

transcript.text: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.
transcript.translation: 事实上，多项研究发现电子书在故事理解和词汇增长方面支持超过印刷书所提供的内容。

transcript.text: But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and the parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
transcript.translation: 但也有研究表明，孩子有时在学习电子书时投入的脑力较少，而且父母在分享这类书时谈论内容较少。

transcript.text: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children.
transcript.translation: 我们今天关注的研究旨在让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿有多好。

transcript.text: For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents.
transcript.translation: 在这项研究中，研究人员录制了17至26个月大的孩子与父母之一一起阅读的视频。

transcript.text: Each parent and child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content.
transcript.translation: 每对父母和孩子被随机分配阅读两本教育电子书或两本内容相同的印刷书。

transcript.text: While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
transcript.translation: 当父母大声朗读印刷书中的文字时，电子书配有配音演员朗读文本的音频。

transcript.text: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，阅读印刷书的父母比阅读电子书的父母更频繁地指向页面。

transcript.text: But the opposite was true for the children.
transcript.translation: 但孩子的情况恰恰相反。

transcript.text: Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
transcript.translation: 阅读电子书的孩子也对内容发表了更多评论，并比阅读印刷书的孩子学到了更多新单词。

transcript.text: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books.
transcript.translation: 这种更多的学习归因于对电子书更大的参与度。

transcript.text: It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple.
transcript.translation: 值得注意的是，研究中的电子书很简单。

transcript.text: While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
transcript.translation: 虽然它们包含了背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外功能。

transcript.text: It's also important to note that there's research on older children finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning.
transcript.translation: 同样值得注意的是，有研究针对年龄较大的儿童发现电子书并不总是能促进学习。

transcript.text: Parents and educators need to beware.
transcript.translation: 父母和教育者需要警惕。

transcript.text: Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them.
transcript.translation: 电子书中的额外功能可能会增加孩子对它们的参与度。

transcript.text: However, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
transcript.translation: 然而，如果这些功能不吸引注意力到教育内容上，它们可能无法起到支持作用。

transcript.text: Let me be honest with you.
transcript.translation: 让我坦诚地告诉你。

transcript.text: If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time.
transcript.translation: 如果你的生活充满遗憾，你就是在浪费时间。

transcript.text: Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today?
transcript.translation: 为什么要一生都在后悔那些造就了今天的你的决定呢？

transcript.text: There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them?
transcript.translation: 我们做过许多不利的决定，但这是否意味着我们应该后悔呢？

transcript.text: No.
transcript.translation: 不。

transcript.text: I've had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently.
transcript.translation: 我曾有许多时刻，坐着回想所有我希望自己能以不同方式处理的事情。

transcript.text: However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better.
transcript.translation: 然而，事情本可以不同，并不一定意味着它们会更好。

transcript.text: You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one.
transcript.translation: 你不必一直思考所有的过去决定以及自己是否做出了正确选择。

transcript.text: You can't go back and change anything.
transcript.translation: 你无法回到过去改变任何事情。

transcript.text: So what's the point in worrying about it?
transcript.translation: 那么担心它又有什么意义呢？

transcript.text: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today.
transcript.translation: 你做出的每一个决定，无论积极还是消极，都造就了今天的你。

transcript.text: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that?
transcript.translation: 我们想回到过去改变部分过去，但那会有什么好处呢？

transcript.text: We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
transcript.translation: 我们将失去从所学教训中获得的宝贵知识。

transcript.text: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are.
transcript.translation: 你做出选择是有原因的，这告诉我们你是谁。

transcript.text: So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself.
transcript.translation: 所以，当涉及到生活中的任何决定时，要毫不犹豫地做自己。

transcript.text: Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
transcript.translation: 因为归根结底，做决定的是你自己。

transcript.text: With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life.
transcript.translation: 花更少的时间专注于遗憾，你最终将有时间专注于生活中更重要的事情。

transcript.text: In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make.
transcript.translation: 在任何情况下，你都会随着每一个决定而成长更多。

transcript.text: Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
transcript.translation: 生活中充满需要学习的教训，所以我们不能让后悔阻止我们前进。

transcript.text: We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made.
transcript.translation: 直到选择做出之后，我们才知道它是否正确。

transcript.text: So it can be easy to start regretting your decision.
transcript.translation: 所以，开始后悔自己的决定是很容易的。

transcript.text: But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it?
transcript.translation: 但如果决定已经做出，纠结于它又有什么目的呢？

transcript.text: There isn't one.
transcript.translation: 没有目的。

transcript.text: All you can do is move forward.
transcript.translation: 你所能做的就是向前看。

transcript.text: You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice.
transcript.translation: 你不能让自己坐在那里为每一个过去的选择担忧。

transcript.text: We aren't all perfect.
transcript.translation: 我们并非完美无缺。

transcript.text: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later.
transcript.translation: 每当你做一个决定，之后总有可能后悔。

transcript.text: But that's how life is supposed to be.
transcript.translation: 但生活本该如此。

transcript.text: You will make poor decisions in life.
transcript.translation: 你一生中会做出糟糕的决定。

transcript.text: We all do.
transcript.translation: 我们都会。

transcript.text: But it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
transcript.translation: 但重要的是你如何处理所学的教训。

transcript.text: Think about every decision you've ever made.
transcript.translation: 想想你曾经做出的每一个决定。

transcript.text: Were they always the best?
transcript.translation: 它们总是最好的吗？

transcript.text: Of course not.
transcript.translation: 当然不是。

transcript.text: But look at how far you've come since then.
transcript.translation: 但看看自那时以来你走了多远。

People __26__ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.

paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, technology has quashed, one by one, claims that __27__ tasks require a human brain. The first adding machine was invented in 1623. This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. I believe the moment when computers meet and __28__ human intelligence is on the horizon.

paragraphs.text: How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? There will likely be a spectrum. In some __29__, people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away.

paragraphs.text: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and __30__. Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic __31__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __32__.

paragraphs.text: And, of course, this question isn't black or white. Many fields will be a __33__, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where, much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __34__ the machines.

paragraphs.text: If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to __35__, that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.

questionGroups.title: Do You Know When to Quit Wisely?

material.title: Do You Know When to Quit Wisely?

paragraphs.text: Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned- and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win," but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.
paragraphs.translation: 项目、人际关系和工作并不总是按计划进行——而且，何时该放弃也并非总是那么清晰。我们都反复听过'放弃者永远不会赢'这句老话，但有时，最好的决定恰恰是及时止损。

paragraphs.text: Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.
paragraphs.translation: 想想那些你明知已走到尽头却依然维系的关系，或是那份让你老板把你折磨得痛苦不堪你却仍坚守的工作。我们中的许多人，都会试图紧抓最后一丝希望，认为自己能让'它'（无论'它'是什么）好转起来。尽管毅力通常是一种极佳的品质，但它也可能诱使你过度投入于某个已不再是好主意的事情上。

paragraphs.text: As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit." But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.
paragraphs.translation: 作为一名高管教练，我与众多充满激情、工作勤奋且不愿'放弃'的领导者共事。但最聪明的领导者懂得辨别'过早放弃'与'执着于本应放弃之事'之间的区别。

paragraphs.text: We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing," you may be especially susceptible to this bias.
paragraphs.translation: 我们都容易受到'沉没成本错觉'的影响，这是一种无意识偏差，会促使我们在已经投入了时间、精力或金钱的事情上继续坚持——即便放弃它会带来更大的好处。我们意识到投入的资源无法收回，因此选择继续坚持——投资于本应中止的项目，维持本应结束的关系，或者读完一本不再享受却已读了一半的书。如果'放弃'不是你的风格，你可能特别容易受到这种偏见的影响。

paragraphs.text: The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?
paragraphs.translation: 沉没成本错觉使我们过分担忧'前进'将失去什么，却未能充分思考'不前进'的代价。为了抵消这种偏见，请有意识地将思考重心转移到'收益'上，以便更客观地权衡各种选择。问问自己：现在及时止损，我可能会得到什么？你会更快乐，还是会有时间去把握另一个（更好的）机会？然后再问自己：继续坚持下去，我会付出什么代价？例如，是否可能在你已经损失的基础上，继续投入更多金钱？或者，你是否会因精力耗尽而无法把握其他有希望的机遇？

paragraphs.text: The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.
paragraphs.translation: 控制错觉也会干扰我们的最佳判断，导致我们高估自己控制事态和取得积极结果的能力。这种偏见给予我们一种掌控感，有益于心理健康。然而，它也可能导致我们不断加大投入，坚持一条注定失败的行动路线。尤其当这种错觉与'我不是半途而废的人'这种心态结合时，感觉自己对某件事或某个人拥有超出实际的掌控力，会在我们本应抽身撤离时，反而让我们选择加倍投入。

paragraphs.text: To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.
paragraphs.translation: 为了对抗这种偏见，请审视你的处境，列一个简单的两栏清单，分别写下哪些是你可以控制的，哪些是不能的。要严谨地思考。虽然你可能能够影响他人和各种环境，但你无法强迫他们改变或按照你的意愿行事。

paragraphs.text: Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.
paragraphs.translation: 弄清楚什么是你能控制的，什么是你不能的，对于做出关于是放弃还是坚持的高质量决策至关重要。手握一份书面清单，能确保你专注于可控之事，并更好地评估你持续的付出是否值得。在不可控的事情上耗费精力和情感，既耗神又令人无力。

paragraphs.text: Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.
paragraphs.translation: 研究表明，人们将他们的自我认同和社会地位与其承诺联系在一起。因为我们认同自己的承诺，所以退出某个承诺可能会让人感觉像是对自我认同或地位的威胁。

paragraphs.text: Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.
paragraphs.translation: 以我的客户瑞安为例，她是一家科技公司的领导者。瑞安在一个设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但该项目并未取得预期的成果，然而，想到要放弃她已经付出的一切，这让她难以接受。当我和瑞安探讨是否应该取消她一直主导的这个项目，还是继续坚持下去时，她说道：'问题是，我不是一个半途而废的人。'这种单一、固化的自我认知蒙蔽了她的判断，限制了她的行动选择。

paragraphs.text: Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."
paragraphs.translation: 我们的自我概念和身份认同是影响我们行为的心理观念。如果你强烈地将自己定义为'不是放弃者'，最终可能会因为这种狭隘而僵化的自我概念而困于某条行动路线中。为了克服这种内在障碍，请回想你其他的积极特质和性格特征。问自己：我还有什么额外的优势（或希望拥有什么优势）可以在这里发挥作用？例如，当我问瑞安，她需要运用性格中的哪些其他积极品质来做决策时，她回答说：'审慎与勇气。'

paragraphs.text: Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.
paragraphs.translation: 现在，通过你自身的这些不同方面来审视你的处境。你内心审慎的部分会说什么？勇敢的部分又会怎么说？通过这些不同的特质来考量你的决策，将使你看到自己拥有更多选择。寻求外部信息来源，而不是仅仅依赖你自己的思考和直觉，也是有帮助的。但重要的是要仔细考虑该征求谁的意见。

paragraphs.text: Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"
paragraphs.translation: 理想情况下，寻找那些对你的决策投入程度低于你的人。例如，如果你正在考虑是否关闭你的创业公司，去联系其他创始人，而不仅仅是你的商业伙伴。同样，如果你正在寻求情感建议，问问一个与你恋爱关系起伏无关的人，而不是只依赖你最好的朋友。在所有情况下，我都建议描述你的情况，然后提出一个类似这样的问题：'你会如何处理这种情况？'

paragraphs.text: Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.
paragraphs.translation: 或者，你也可以寻找能够揭示你在所考虑的任何努力中真实成功概率的硬数据。继续以创业公司为例，数字是你最好的朋友。用它们来让你跳出对这个想法的热爱，从消耗率相对于增长计划、行业增长率以及其他预测创业成功的因素的角度来考虑。外部信息来源可以帮助你看到自己可能未曾考虑过的角度和可能性。

paragraphs.text: When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience, emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.
paragraphs.translation: 当某个起初看似充满希望的事情并未如我们想象般发展时，我们可能会变得过度自责。没有人喜欢感觉自己做出了糟糕的决定，尤其是当你高度重视'做出明智决策'这一品质时。此时最有效的策略是放过自己。练习自我关怀可以增强你的韧性、情商、对他人的同情心，并能提升你的表现，同时也有助于你培养成长型心态。

paragraphs.text: Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.
paragraphs.translation: 与其反复斟酌和批评自己，不如专注于你能从这种情况中学到什么。例如，瑞安认识到，通过领导这个设计项目，她发展了多种新技能和领导能力。尽管最终决定放弃它，她仍然为自己尝试过而感到高兴，并对这段经历教会她的东西心存感激。

paragraphs.text: Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your wellbeing, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.
paragraphs.translation: 不可否认，毅力可以帮助我们成功。但为了你的福祉，学会区分'过早放弃'和'执着于一条失败的行动路线'非常重要。虽然放手可能很困难，但它将为你的时间、精力和思维空间腾出余地，去想象新的可能性，追求新的机遇。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: Feeling like they have more control over something or someone than they do, people get more committed to their pursuit when they should give up.
questions.analysis: F段指出控制幻觉（illusion of control）会让人高估自己控制事件的能力，尤其与「我不是放弃者」的心态结合时，会导致人们在本应退出时加倍投入。题目中的关键信息与F段末句完全对应。

questions.statementText: If you regard yourself as one who never quits, you may end up trapped in your course of action.
questions.analysis: K段明确指出，如果你强烈认同自己不是一个放弃者（strongly identify as not being a quitter），你可能会因为狭隘和僵化的自我概念而困在某个行动方案中（staying stuck）。题目是对该段核心观点的同义转述。

questions.statementText: One of the author's clients found it hard to give up a design project, in which she had put in a lot of time and effort.
questions.analysis: J段以客户Ryan为例，描述她在一个设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但项目未能达到预期成果，放弃它对她来说很难承受。题目中的关键细节（design project、time and effort、hard to give up）均出自J段。

questions.statementText: The author suggests that one should direct their thoughts to the gains of quitting timely so as to move on.
questions.analysis: E段建议刻意将思维重新聚焦在收益上（deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains），以便更客观地权衡各种选择，从而克服沉没成本偏见、做到及时止损。题目中direct thoughts to gains与E段的refocus thinking on gains对应。

questions.statementText: When making a decision, you'd better ask for opinions of those who have less stake in your decision.
questions.analysis: M段建议寻求那些对你的决定投入较少的人的意见（people who are less invested in your decision），题目中的less stake与原文的less invested是同义表达。

questions.statementText: For people associating their identity with their commitments, quitting can feel like their identity is threatened.
questions.analysis: I段指出研究表明人们将自我认同和社会地位与自己的承诺挂钩（link their self-identity and social status to their commitments），因此退出某项承诺会让人感到身份或地位受到威胁。题目是对I段内容的准确概括。

questions.statementText: People who regard highly the quality of making wise decisions do not feel good when they make a bad one.
questions.analysis: O段提到没有人喜欢觉得自己做了糟糕的决定，尤其是那些高度重视做出明智决定这一品质的人（making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem）。题目中regard highly与hold in high esteem同义。

questions.statementText: The wisest leaders learn to distinguish between giving up too soon and sticking with something irrationally.
questions.analysis: C段指出最聪明的领导者学会区分过早放弃和不应该坚持的事情（discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't）。题目中的sticking with something irrationally对应holding onto something they shouldn't。

questions.statementText: When people are thinking of an endeavor, they should dig out reliable data that tells them how likely they are to succeed.
questions.analysis: N段建议寻找硬数据来评估在某项事业中的真实成功几率（seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success）。题目中的dig out reliable data与seek out hard data对应，how likely to succeed与real chance of success对应。

questions.statementText: Having a clear view of what's in your control and what's not is vital to making a good decision regarding whether to give up or stick it out.
questions.analysis: H段开头明确指出，弄清楚什么在你的控制范围内、什么不在，对于做出是否放弃或坚持的高质量决定至关重要（Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision）。题目几乎是原文的同义转述。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organised ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organisations, and families.
paragraphs.translation: 作为相互依存的生物，我们无法脱离他人而茁壮成长。我们喜欢与志同道合、拥有共同兴趣或同样认真相信某一事业的人一起工作。这体现在我们如何将自己组织成各种集体群体，如国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭。

paragraphs.text: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
paragraphs.translation: 你所属的群体是否有强烈的集体意识或共同信仰？成员之间是否存在相互依存关系？你是否认为这个群体是你存在的重要部分？如果答案是肯定的，那么你正在体验一种微观版本的团结。

paragraphs.text: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "...a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."
paragraphs.translation: 什么是团结？词典中最简单的定义是：“……一群人的统一意见、情感、目的或利益。”

paragraphs.text: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labour.
paragraphs.translation: 在我们生活的这个日益多样化的社会中，团结呈现出复杂和多面的特征，因为它在生活在快速变化环境中、从事复杂分工的独特个体之间形成了相互依存的纽带。

paragraphs.text: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism. In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy is sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
paragraphs.translation: 团结的一个方面与社群主义的原则非常契合。在这种背景下，个体放弃自己的利益以服务共同利益。然而，它对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格坚持限制了个人差异和偏好的表达与实践。因此，个性和自主性被牺牲以维护群体的统一。

paragraphs.text: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
paragraphs.translation: 团结也被视为对极端强调个人主义和选择自由的一种反应。它反对自由主义的观点，即无约束的个体认为社会是阻碍他们自由选择并根据自身利益行动的障碍，而不管这些行为如何影响他人。

paragraphs.text: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterised by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.
paragraphs.translation: 但尽管团结有许多方面，社会理论家认为它是带来社会秩序和进步的关键因素。他们相信，随着人类社会变得更加多样化，需要基于差异形成更多新的纽带。鉴于此，他们认为真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的浅层关系。团结不仅仅是战略计算自身受益多少的产物。它不是一个基于“你我对抗世界”原则的排他性阶层。相反，它是包容的，并且不被强迫。出于团结的行动意味着相互支持和捍卫——认识到自己的命运与他人的命运相连。这是一种以合作实践为特征、以对他人或共同利益福祉的关切为加强的纽带。它为保护人类尊严而奋斗，并倾听和回应最脆弱者的呼声。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C), and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What does the author say about human beings?

options.label: A
options.text: They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other.

options.label: B
options.text: They share a common interest and believe in a just cause.

options.label: C
options.text: They think and behave alike in different social groups.

options.label: D
options.text: They cannot gain independence without fighting for it.

questions.analysis: 文章开篇指出人类是相互依存的存在，不能脱离他人而繁荣（As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others）。A选项中的cannot prosper without cooperating是对原文的同义转述。thrive对应prosper，interdependent对应cooperating with each other。
questions.keySentence: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.

wrongOptions.B: 原文说人们喜欢与志同道合的人合作，但并非说所有人类都共享共同利益和信仰，这是对原文的过度概括。
wrongOptions.C: 原文没有说人们在不同社会群体中思维和行为方式相同，而是说人们倾向于与志同道合的人合作。
wrongOptions.D: 原文讨论的是相互依存而非独立，且没有提到为独立而斗争的内容。

questions.questionText: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society?

options.label: A
options.text: It gives rise to a complicated division of labour.

options.label: B
options.text: It involves many aspects with great complexity.

options.label: C
options.text: It brings individuals together as environment changes.

options.label: D
options.text: It embraces the characteristics of different individuals.

questions.analysis: 第四段指出在日益多元化的社会中，团结具有复杂和多面的特征（a complex and multifaceted character）。B选项中的many aspects对应multifaceted，great complexity对应complex，是原文的准确转述。
questions.keySentence: solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labour.

wrongOptions.A: 原文说团结在复杂分工中形成纽带，但不是说团结导致了复杂的分工，因果关系被颠倒了。
wrongOptions.C: 原文虽然提到环境变化和个体之间的纽带，但B选项更准确地概括了该段的核心信息——团结的复杂多面性。
wrongOptions.D: 原文提到unique individuals，但并没有说团结拥抱了不同个体的特征，这是对原文的曲解。

questions.questionText: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism?

options.label: A
options.text: Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality.

options.label: B
options.text: Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences.

options.label: C
options.text: Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good.

options.label: D
options.text: Elimination of individualism and personal choices.

questions.analysis: 第五段明确指出，在社群主义的背景下，个人放弃自己的利益来服务于公共利益（individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good）。C选项是对这句话的直接转述，sacrifice对应give up，personal interests对应own interests。
questions.keySentence: In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.

wrongOptions.A: 虽然原文提到个体性和自主性被牺牲，但并没有说社会规范占统治地位，ridding of individuality也过于极端。
wrongOptions.B: 与原文相反，社群主义限制了个体差异的表达和实践（restricts expression and practice of individual differences），而非强调对个体差异的坚持。
wrongOptions.D: 原文说的是个体性和自主性被牺牲以维护团体统一，但elimination过于绝对，且原文用的是sacrificed而非eliminated。

questions.questionText: What does solidarity entail according to the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: A limit to personal differences.

options.label: B
options.text: An opposition to individualism.

options.label: C
options.text: A hindrance to social advancement.

options.label: D
options.text: An inevitable end to liberal pursuits.

questions.analysis: 第六段指出团结也被视为对极端个人主义和选择自由的过度强调的一种回应（a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism）。它反对不受约束的个人将社会视为自由障碍的自由主义观点。B选项中的opposition to individualism准确概括了这一含义。
questions.keySentence: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.

wrongOptions.A: 限制个人差异是社群主义的特征（第五段），而非团结本身的含义，属于张冠李戴。
wrongOptions.C: 原文最后一段指出社会理论家认为团结是促进社会秩序和进步的关键因素，与「阻碍社会进步」完全相反。
wrongOptions.D: 原文说团结是对极端个人主义的回应，但并没有说它必然终结自由主义追求，inevitable end过于绝对。

questions.questionText: What do social theorists think of solidarity?

options.label: A
options.text: It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable.

options.label: B
options.text: It is most effective in protecting human dignity.

options.label: C
options.text: It is essential to progress and order in society.

options.label: D
options.text: It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships.

questions.analysis: 最后一段开头明确指出社会理论家将团结视为带来社会秩序和进步的关键因素（a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society）。C选项中essential to progress and order是对原文key factor in bringing about order and progress的同义转述。
questions.keySentence: social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.

wrongOptions.A: 原文最后提到团结关注最弱势群体的呼声，但这是对真正团结的描述，而非社会理论家对团结的核心评价。
wrongOptions.B: 保护人类尊严是团结的一个功能，但社会理论家的核心观点是团结对社会秩序和进步至关重要，B选项以偏概全。
wrongOptions.D: 原文提到真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的浅层关系，但这是在区分真正团结与非真正团结，而非说团结的本质是避免浅层关系。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
paragraphs.translation: 那些反复提供不请自来建议的人可能出于好意，真心想帮助他人。另一些人可能这样做是出于一种自我价值感，即影响他人的能力。一项研究发现，寻求权力倾向高的人比倾向相反的人更可能提供建议。

paragraphs.text: Under the guise of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
paragraphs.translation: 在无私的表象下，人们可能被驱使给你不请自来的建议，因为这让他们感到强大或掌控。然而，他们可能没有完全意识到这种驱动力。

paragraphs.text: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
paragraphs.translation: 这些人还可能表现出有问题的情绪脆弱性，很快变得心烦意乱，并需要很长时间才能平静下来。可能他们的情绪只有在童年时期当他们最为激烈时才得到认可，这鼓励了他们采用在大多数情况下过度的不适反应。

paragraphs.text: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesirable result.
paragraphs.translation: 当某人为了让自己感觉更强大而提供建议时，他们的行为中存在着接收者往往会注意到的潜在焦虑。在这种情况下，严厉回应建议者并指责他们操纵他人可能很诱人，但这种方法可能产生不良结果。

paragraphs.text: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
paragraphs.translation: 如果提供建议的行为积极促进了某人的自我价值感，那么彻底拒绝可能被视为威胁，激活他们的战斗或逃跑反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求认可的行为，或引发更大的冲突。

paragraphs.text: The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"
paragraphs.translation: 关键是认可而不过度认同。你可以让他们知道你听到了他们的话并欣赏他们的出发点，而不接受那种可能有害的叙事，即没有他们的帮助你无法应对。你最好说类似这样的话：“谢谢你的想法。我有自己的处理计划，但我真的很欣赏你的观点，会加以考虑。将来我需要帮助时可以告诉你吗？”

paragraphs.text: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你在巧妙设定界限方面有困难，请优先提升自我调节能力。尽管不断收到不请自来的建议可能让你不舒服，但如果你能以同情心回应，情况可能会更快缓解。

paragraphs.text: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管这通常不是提供不请自来建议的预期结果，但许多接收者常常因这些建议感到压力、冒犯或 simply annoyed。在这方面设定界限，如果你觉得需要，是完全合理的，并且能带来更大的情感安全感。

paragraphs.text: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
paragraphs.translation: 最好以考虑个人行为背后原因的方式设定界限，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C), and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What is the finding of one study about people who keep giving unsolicited advice?

options.label: A
options.text: They turn out to be well-meaning.

options.label: B
options.text: They are genuinely kind-hearted.

options.label: C
options.text: They are capable of influencing others.

options.label: D
options.text: They are inclined to crave for power.

questions.analysis: 第一段提到一项研究发现，那些有强烈寻求权力倾向的人更可能给出建议（people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice）。D选项中的inclined to crave for power对应原文的high tendency to seek power。
questions.keySentence: One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.

wrongOptions.A: 原文提到有些不请自来的建议者可能是出于好意，但这不是研究的发现，而是一般性描述。
wrongOptions.B: 原文说有些人genuinely want to help，但这同样不是研究发现的内容，研究发现的是与权力寻求倾向的关系。
wrongOptions.C: 原文提到影响他人的能力（ability to influence others），但这是描述给出建议者的自我价值感来源，而非研究发现。

questions.questionText: What is the problem with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice?

options.label: A
options.text: They may be quick to upset others.

options.label: B
options.text: They may be emotionally vulnerable.

options.label: C
options.text: They want their voice to be the loudest.

options.label: D
options.text: They respond to discomfort excessively.

questions.analysis: 第三段指出这些人可能表现出一种有问题的情感脆弱程度（a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability），很快就会变得不安，且需要很长时间才能平静下来。B选项直接对应原文的emotional vulnerability。
questions.keySentence: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.

wrongOptions.A: 原文说的是他们自己很快变得不安（becoming upset very quickly），而不是快速惹怒他人，A选项偷换了主语。
wrongOptions.C: 原文提到他们的情绪在童年时只有在最响亮时才被认可，但这是解释行为成因，而非说他们现在想让自己的声音最大。
wrongOptions.D: 对不适的过度反应是描述他们行为的一个方面，但问题的核心是情感脆弱性，D选项未能抓住核心问题。

questions.questionText: What is the advice receiver tempted to do when noticing the advice giver's underlying anxiety?

options.label: A
options.text: Reveal the undesirable result of their approach.

options.label: B
options.text: Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner.

options.label: C
options.text: Bring their real motives to the surface.

options.label: D
options.text: Accuse them of trying to control others.

questions.analysis: 第四段指出，当建议接收者注意到建议者的潜在焦虑时，很容易会对建议者做出严厉回应并指责他们具有操控性（accuse them of being manipulative）。D选项中的accuse them of trying to control others是对being manipulative的同义转述。
questions.keySentence: It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative

wrongOptions.A: 原文提到这种做法可能产生不良结果（undesirable result），但这是对harsh reaction后果的描述，而非建议接收者想要做的事。
wrongOptions.B: 原文没有提到以直白方式拒绝建议，而是说指责对方具有操控性。
wrongOptions.C: 虽然指责对方manipulative暗示了揭露动机，但原文明确使用的是accuse them of being manipulative，重点在于指责操控行为而非揭露动机。

questions.questionText: How is the advice giver likely to react to the rejection of their advice?

options.label: A
options.text: They may regard it as a threat.

options.label: B
options.text: They may modify their behavior.

options.label: C
options.text: They get ready for a larger conflict.

options.label: D
options.text: They begin to doubt their self-worth.

questions.analysis: 第五段指出，如果给建议这个行为积极地支撑着某人的自我价值感，那么直接拒绝可能被视为一种威胁（an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat）。A选项中的regard it as a threat直接对应原文的perceived as a threat。
questions.keySentence: an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response

wrongOptions.B: 原文说的是他们可能会加倍寻求认可的行为（double down on their validation-seeking behavior），而非修正行为，恰恰相反。
wrongOptions.C: 原文提到可能导致更大的冲突（leading to a larger conflict），但这是拒绝可能带来的后果，而非建议者有意为之的反应。
wrongOptions.D: 原文说给建议有助于他们的自我价值感，拒绝被视为威胁，但并没有说他们会开始怀疑自己的价值，而是会产生战斗或逃跑反应。

questions.questionText: What should the advice receiver do to avoid unnecessary conflict?

options.label: A
options.text: Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable.

options.label: B
options.text: Give their reasons for not taking the advice.

options.label: C
options.text: Understand why the advice giver offers the advice.

options.label: D
options.text: Explain their chosen way of handling the situation.

questions.analysis: 文章最后一段指出，最好以考虑到对方行为背后原因的方式来设定边界（takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing），以避免不必要的冲突。C选项中的understand why对应takes into account the underlying reasons。
questions.keySentence: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

wrongOptions.A: 原文建议认可对方的观点（validate），但并非承认建议本身完全合理，而是表示你听到了他们的意见并理解他们的出发点。
wrongOptions.B: 原文没有建议解释不接受建议的原因，而是建议理解对方给出建议的深层原因。
wrongOptions.D: 虽然示例对话中提到了自己有处理问题的计划，但文章最后总结的核心建议是理解对方行为的深层原因，而非解释自己的处理方式。

questionGroups.sourceText: 中华民族崇尚自强自立的精神，这一精神深植于中国文化之中，是民族生存与发展的重要支撑。改革开放以来，中国在自强自立的征程上，持续加大科研投入，在信息技术、人工智能、航天工程等领域不断取得新突破。5G网络覆盖全国，远程医疗发展迅速，电子支付的使用全球领先，嫦娥探月工程展现了航天领域引人注目的发展。自强自立精神成为推动国家现代化进程的强大动力，激励着中国人民为实现民族复兴的中国梦不断奋进。
